title: API Platform, Governance, and Developer Experience Engineering
stage: Operate APIs as an organizational platform
centralQuestion: How can an organization make trustworthy API work easier to discover, create, publish, consume, evolve, support, and retire without centralizing domain ownership?
responsibility: Turn the interfaces, evidence, and ownership model from Courses 1–9 into a product-oriented API platform with governed self-service and measurable consumer outcomes.
incomingBoundary: The Course 9 handoff containing HTTP, event, RPC, distributed-service, and GraphQL contracts with explicit ownership and release evidence.
outgoingBoundary: Analysis API Platform 1.0, a governed catalog and registry, lifecycle and policy engine, golden path, documentation and sandbox, SDK and provenance publication, runtime reconciliation, support model, and a ten-course graduation dossier.
versionState: All earlier interface and engineering profiles preserved; Analysis API Platform 1.0 and platform-catalog metadata migrations 001–004 introduced.
languageStrategy: one primary implementation track plus one comparative reference track

modules.title: Platform Product Model and Operating Boundaries
modules.centralQuestion: Which recurring problems should an API platform own, and which decisions must stay with domain teams?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish the platform product charter, user journeys, ownership boundary, and initial outcome model.
learningOutcomes: define the platform as a product with distinct users
separate essential domain decisions from accidental repeated work
establish platform, domain, and governance ownership
evaluate paved roads and justified exceptions
choose outcome metrics instead of feature counts

modules.title: Catalog, Ownership Graph, and Metadata Authority
modules.centralQuestion: How can a central catalog be useful without pretending to own every fact it displays?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish the Analysis Platform catalog and ownership graph.
learningOutcomes: model components, APIs, resources, systems, domains, and groups
assign canonical identity and accountable ownership
separate authoritative, derived, and observed metadata
validate relations and detect orphans
use the graph for impact and support analysis

modules.title: Contract Registry and Multi-Protocol Publication
modules.centralQuestion: What makes an API contract a trustworthy published release across HTTP, events, RPC, and GraphQL?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Register the four inherited interface releases by digest and publication evidence.
learningOutcomes: distinguish drafts, releases, channels, and promotions
bind releases to exact bytes and owners
preserve protocol-native contracts
attach protocol-appropriate compatibility evidence
reject mutable release identities

modules.title: Governance as Code, Evidence, Scorecards, and Exceptions
modules.centralQuestion: How can governance scale without becoming either a rubber stamp or a centralized release bottleneck?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish the policy pack, evidence ledger, exception register, and release scorecards.
learningOutcomes: design deterministic policy rules around authoritative evidence
preserve pass, review, and fail semantics
build evidence-backed scorecards without vanity averages
model temporary exceptions and compensating controls
federate policy ownership across platform and domain teams

modules.title: Lifecycle, Compatibility, Deprecation, and Retirement
modules.centralQuestion: How can an API evolve and eventually disappear without transferring hidden cost to consumers?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish the lifecycle policy, consumer inventory, deprecation impact report, and retirement decision.
learningOutcomes: model lifecycle as evidence-gated transitions
build a multi-source consumer inventory
design migration and notice workflows
block unsafe retirement
preserve historical contract truth

modules.title: Golden Paths, Templates, and Self-Service Provisioning
modules.centralQuestion: How can a platform reduce repeated setup work without hiding essential engineering decisions or creating clone-and-forget debt?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish and verify the `api-capability-v1` golden path and generated reference fixture.
learningOutcomes: design a golden path as a maintained product
choose safe defaults and essential parameters
render deterministically and atomically
include ownership, tests, docs, and governance hooks
govern upgrades and supported escape hatches

modules.title: Documentation, Discovery, Sandboxes, and Consumer Onboarding
modules.centralQuestion: Can a new consumer find the right interface, trust it, and complete a useful workflow safely without private organizational knowledge?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish the task-oriented portal source, search index, sandbox profile, and first-success evidence.
learningOutcomes: organize documentation around tasks and interface choice
publish trustworthy discovery metadata
build executable version-bound examples
design isolated synthetic sandboxes
measure onboarding outcomes and route support

modules.title: SDKs, CLIs, Artifacts, SBOMs, and Provenance
modules.centralQuestion: How can developer artifacts remain convenient, idiomatic, reproducible, and traceable to the contracts that produced them?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish Python and TypeScript client artifacts with contract identity, SBOM, and bounded provenance evidence.
learningOutcomes: design SDKs as supported products rather than raw generated code
link packages to exact contract releases
distinguish SBOM, provenance, checksum, and signature evidence
govern package versioning and retention
reject untraceable or misleading publication claims

modules.title: Runtime Control Plane, Usage Intelligence, and Support Operations
modules.centralQuestion: How can platform metadata remain connected to the running system and to consumer outcomes without becoming a new domain owner or surveillance system?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Publish runtime desired state, drift proof, product metrics, and support routing evidence.
learningOutcomes: reconcile approved releases with runtime routes
keep edge and domain policy boundaries explicit
measure onboarding, adoption, migration, and support outcomes
route support through authoritative ownership
apply privacy and cardinality limits to platform analytics

modules.title: Federated Governance, Platform Operations, and Final Defense
modules.centralQuestion: How can the platform scale across an organization while remaining useful, operable, accountable, and subordinate to domain ownership?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Complete and defend Analysis API Platform 1.0 and the ten-course API Engineering program.
learningOutcomes: design a federated platform operating model
apply SLO and lifecycle discipline to the platform itself
focus central review on novel risk
drive adoption through measurable value
defend Analysis API Platform 1.0 across all user perspectives
